lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: Experience is not listed in reverse chronological order.
items.because: Clearwater Sensors appears above the more recent Voltline Robotics role, delaying the reader’s view of the embedded-software work.

items.says: The Formula Student project should be shortened to a compact supporting entry.
items.because: It is older and gives substantial space to claims that overlap with the later robotics experience.

items.says: The 10-month period between graduation and the first listed job is unexplained.
“Automated end-of-line tests” does not show how the automation was implemented.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what technical capability the work required.

items.says: The strongest Clearwater Sensors achievement should lead the entry.
The calibration-procedure bullet does not describe the procedure’s technical content.
items.because: The reader cannot see the engineering judgment behind the reduction in drift complaints.

items.says: “Improved update speed by 60%” does not identify the measured metric or baseline.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether it refers to installation time, download time, or throughput.

items.says: The hardware-in-the-loop test-rig bullet does not state what changed as a result.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether it caught regressions, shortened validation, or improved release confidence.

items.says: “Which found the root cause” gives the crash logger agency.
items.because: It obscures that the captured data enabled the investigation.

items.says: An 8 kHz sampling rate cannot capture the stated 5 kHz signal without aliasing.
items.because: Its 4 kHz Nyquist frequency is below the stated signal frequency.

items.says: The sampling bullet states an intended capability but no resulting improvement.
items.because: The reader cannot see whether fault detection became more accurate, sensitive, or useful in a missed case.

items.says: Declaring the shared counter volatile does not by itself fix the race condition.
items.because: It does not make increments atomic or provide mutual exclusion.

items.says: The race-condition bullet gives no result beyond the code change.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what failure the fix eliminated.

items.says: The motor-controller rewrite duplicates the distinctive accomplishment claimed in the Formula Student project.
items.because: The entries place nearly identical results and roughly 300 robots in different roles and periods.

items.says: The opening weather-station bullet uses promotional, generic language instead of engineering work or a concrete result.
items.because: It reads as marketing rather than evidence of embedded-systems capability.

items.says: The strongest weather-station result should lead the entry.
“Average current” omits the measurement conditions or duty cycle.
The school-built-stations result does not explain what the adoption enabled or demonstrated.
“Published ... openly” is redundant and imprecise.
The bullet incorrectly assigns robot-fleet motor-controller work to the Formula Student project.
items.because: The project concerns a race car, and the same robot work appears under Voltline Robotics.

items.says: “Worked on firmware and testing” gives no specific contribution or outcome.
items.because: It does not show what you developed, modified, or tested, or prove its value.

items.says: The passive dashboard CAN-bus bullet obscures your ownership.
The dashboard CAN-bus bullet does not state what the work enabled or improved.
The Formula Student bullet incorrectly claims a rewrite for a fleet of about 300 robots.
items.because: The claim fits the later robotics role and repeats its distinctive motor-control result.

items.says: “Rewrote motor-control firmware” does not identify the technical approach.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether the improvement came from scheduling, control-loop design, communication, or fault handling.

items.says: “Cutting control-loop jitter eightfold” is ambiguous.
items.because: It can mean reduced to one-eighth or reduced by eight times.

items.says: The relative results do not identify the testing context or measurement period.
items.because: The reader cannot assess whether they came from controlled testing, race data, or another period.

items.says: The Formula Student entry is loosely ordered, opening with a broad task before its more consequential firmware result.
C++ is listed without evidence of C++ work elsewhere in the résumé.
Oscilloscopes are listed without evidence of their use in the entries.
